<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>I</c>ubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Exsultémus Dómino.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
b.0ff8d9d577:
<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>L</c>et us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us glorify the Lord.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.

De libro primo Regum
<r>1 Reg 8:19-21</r>
<n>19</n> Nóluit autem pópulus audíre vocem Samuélis, sed dixérunt: Nequáquam: rex enim erit super nos,
<n>20</n> Et érimus nos quoque sicut omnes gentes: et iudicábit nos rex noster, et egrediétur ante nos, et pugnábit bella nostra pro nobis.
<n>21</n> Et audívit Sámuel ómnia verba pópuli, et locútus est ea in áuribus Dómini.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Deus ómnium exaudítor est: ipse misit Angelum suum, et tulit me de óvibus patris mei:
* Et unxit me unctióne misericórdiæ suæ.
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus, qui erípuit me de ore leónis, et de manu béstiæ liberávit me.
<r>℟.</r> Et unxit me unctióne misericórdiæ suæ.

<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:

b.4c3a4c80eb:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>S</c>exto Idus Iúnii Luna quarta. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>A</h>quis, in Gállia, sancti Maximíni, qui éxstitit primus eiúsdem civitátis Epíscopus, ac Dómini discípulus fuísse tráditur.
<h>E</h>ódem die sanctæ Callíopæ Mártyris, quæ, ob Christi fidem, abscíssis mammis atque adústis cárnibus, super téstulas volutáta, demum, truncáta cápite, martýrii palmam accépit.
<h>E</h>boráci, in Anglia, sancti Willhélmi, Epíscopi et Confessóris, qui, inter cétera ad eius sepúlcrum patráta mirácula, tres mórtuos suscitávit, atque ab Honório Papa Tértio in Sanctórum cánonem relátus est.
<h>A</h>pud Suessiónes, in Gálliis, natális sancti Medárdi, Epíscopi Novioménsis; cuius vita et mors pretiósa gloriósis miráculis commendátur.
<h>R</h>otómagi sancti Gildárdi Epíscopi, qui fuit frater eiúsdem sancti Medárdi. Ambo autem fratres, eódem die nati eodémque die Epíscopi consecráti, uno quoque die de hac vita subtrácti, simul in cælum migrárunt.
<h>A</h>pud Senónas sancti Heráclii Epíscopi.
<h>M</h>etis, in Gállia, sancti Clodúlphi Epíscopi.
<h>I</h>n Picéno sancti Severíni, Septempedáni Epíscopi.
<h>I</h>n Sardínia sancti Sallustiáni Confessóris.
<h>C</h>ameríni sancti Victoríni Confessóris, qui fuit prædícti sancti Severíni, Septempedáni Epíscopi, germánus frater.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.2e9571bb09:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>une 8th 2027, the 4th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Aix in France, St. Maximin, first bishop of that city, who is said to have been a disciple of the Lord.
<h>O</h>n the same day, St. Calliopa, martyr, who for the faith of Christ received the palm of martyrdom. Her breasts had been cut away, her flesh burned, she was rolled on broken pottery, and was at last beheaded.
<h>A</h>t York in England, St. William, archbishop and confessor, who, among other miracles wrought at his tomb, raised three persons from the dead. He was placed in the calendar of the saints by Pope Honorius III.
<h>A</h>t Soissons in France, the birthday of St. Medard, bishop of Noyon, whose life and precious death are commended by glorious miracles.
<h>A</h>t Rouen, St. Gildard, bishop, brother of this same St. Medard. They were born on the same day, consecrated bishops at the same time, and were taken from this life on the same day, entering heaven together.
<h>A</h>t Sens, the bishop St. Heraclius.
<h>A</h>t Metz, the bishop St. Clodulph.
<h>I</h>n Piceno, St. Severin, bishop of Septempeda.
<h>I</h>n Sardinia, St. Sallustian, confessor.
<h>A</h>t Camerino, St. Victorinus, confessor, the twin brother of St. Severin, bishop of Septempeda.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
